units.zh: 滕曇恭
units.en: Teng Tangong
units.literal: Teng Tangong

units.zh: 滕曇恭，豫章南昌人也。
units.en: Teng Tangong came from Nanchang in Yuzhang.
units.literal: Teng Tangong came from Nanchang in Yuzhang.

units.zh: 年五歲，母楊氏患熱，思食寒瓜，土俗所不產。
units.en: When he was five, his mother, Lady Yang, suffered from a fever and longed to eat cold melon, but the local custom did not produce it.
units.literal: When he was five, his mother, Lady Yang, suffered from a fever and longed to eat cold melon, but the local custom did not produce it.

units.zh: 曇恭歷訪不能得，銜悲哀切。
units.en: Tangong searched everywhere but could not obtain any, and he held grief in his heart with deep sorrow.
units.literal: Tangong searched everywhere but could not obtain any, and he held grief in his heart with deep sorrow.

units.zh: 俄值一桑門問其故，曇恭具以告。
units.en: Soon he encountered a Buddhist monk who asked the reason, and Tangong told him everything.
units.literal: Soon he encountered a Buddhist monk who asked the reason, and Tangong told him everything.

units.zh: 桑門曰：「我有兩瓜，分一相遺。」
units.en: The monk said, "I have two melons; I will give you one of them."
units.literal: The monk said, "I have two melons; I will give you one of them."

units.zh: 曇恭拜謝，因捧瓜還，以薦其母。
units.en: Tangong bowed in thanks, then carried the melon home and presented it to his mother.
units.literal: Tangong bowed in thanks, then carried the melon home and presented it to his mother.

units.zh: 舉室驚異。
units.en: The whole household was amazed.
units.literal: The whole household was amazed.

units.zh: 尋訪桑門，莫知所在。
units.en: When they soon searched for the monk, no one knew where he was.
units.literal: When they soon searched for the monk, no one knew where he was.

units.zh: 及父母卒，曇恭水漿不入口者旬日，感慟嘔血，絕而復蘇。
units.en: When his parents died, Tangong took neither water nor gruel for ten days; overcome with grief, he vomited blood, lost consciousness, and then revived.
units.literal: When his parents died, Tangong took neither water nor gruel for ten days; overcome with grief, he vomited blood, lost consciousness, and then revived.

units.zh: 隆冬不著繭絮，蔬食終身。
units.en: In the depth of winter he wore no padded silk or floss, and he ate vegetables for the rest of his life.
units.literal: In the depth of winter he wore no padded silk or floss, and he ate vegetables for the rest of his life.

units.zh: 每至忌日，思慕不自堪，晝夜哀慟。
units.en: Whenever the death anniversaries arrived, longing overcame him, and he wailed in grief day and night.
units.literal: Whenever the death anniversaries arrived, longing overcame him, and he wailed in grief day and night.

units.zh: 其門外有冬生樹二株，時忽有神光自樹而起，俄見佛像及夾侍之儀，容光顯著，自門而入。
units.en: Outside his gate stood two winter-growing trees. At one point divine light suddenly rose from the trees, and soon a Buddha image and attendant figures appeared, their radiant forms clearly visible, entering through the gate.
units.literal: Outside his gate stood two winter-growing trees. At one point divine light suddenly rose from the trees, and soon a Buddha image and attendant figures appeared, their radiant forms clearly visible, entering through the gate.

units.zh: 曇恭家人大小，咸共禮拜，久之乃滅，遠近道俗咸傳之。
units.en: All the members of Tangong's household, great and small, bowed in worship together; after a long while it vanished, and Daoists, Buddhists, and laypeople far and near all passed on the story.
units.literal: All the members of Tangong's household, great and small, bowed in worship together; after a long while it vanished, and Daoists, Buddhists, and laypeople far and near all passed on the story.

units.zh: 太守王僧度引曇恭爲功曹，固辭不就。
units.en: Administrator Wang Sengdu summoned Tangong to serve as merit officer, but he firmly declined and did not take the post.
units.literal: Administrator Wang Sengdu summoned Tangong to serve as merit officer, but he firmly declined and did not take the post.

units.zh: 王儉時隨僧度在郡，號爲滕曾子。
units.en: Wang Jian was then in the commandery with Sengdu and called him Teng Zengzi.
units.literal: Wang Jian was then in the commandery with Sengdu and called him Teng Zengzi.

units.zh: 天監元年，陸璉奉使巡行風俗，表言其狀。
units.en: In Tianjian 1, Lu Lian received an imperial mission to inspect local customs and submitted a memorial describing Tangong's conduct.
units.literal: In Tianjian 1, Lu Lian received an imperial mission to inspect local customs and submitted a memorial describing Tangong's conduct.

units.zh: 曇恭有子三人，皆有行業。
units.en: Tangong had three sons, all of whom had virtuous conduct.
units.literal: Tangong had three sons, all of whom had virtuous conduct.

units.zh: 徐普濟
units.en: Xu Puji
units.literal: Xu Puji

units.zh: 時有徐普濟者，長沙臨湘人。
units.en: There was Xu Puji of Linxiang, Changsha.
units.literal: At that time there was Xu Puji, a man of Linxiang in Changsha.

units.zh: 居喪未及葬，而鄰家火起，延及其舍，普濟號慟伏棺上，以身蔽火。
units.en: Before the funeral a neighbor's fire reached his house; Puji cried out and lay on the coffin, covering it with his body.
units.literal: While in mourning before the burial, a neighbor's house caught fire and the blaze spread to his dwelling; Puji wailed and threw himself on the coffin, shielding it with his body.

units.zh: 鄰人往救之，焚炙已悶絕，累日方蘇。
units.en: Neighbors pulled him away; the burns had already stunned him breathless, and only after days did he wake.
units.literal: Neighbors came to rescue him; he had already been scorched and suffocated, and only after several days did he revive.

units.zh: 宛陵女子
units.en: The woman of Wanling
units.literal: The woman of Wanling

units.zh: 宣城宛陵有女子與母同床寢，母爲猛虎所搏，女號叫拿虎，虎毛盡落，行十數里，虎乃棄之。
units.en: At Wanling in Xuancheng a woman shared a bed with her mother; a tiger seized the mother and the daughter shrieked, seized the beast, and tore its fur away; after ten-odd li the tiger dropped her.
units.literal: In Xuancheng's Wanling a woman slept in the same bed with her mother; a fierce tiger seized the mother, and the daughter screamed and grappled with the tiger until its fur fell out; after more than ten li the tiger at last abandoned her.

units.zh: 女抱母還，猶有氣，經時乃絕。
units.en: She carried her mother home; breath remained awhile, then ceased.
units.literal: The daughter carried her mother back; she still had breath, but after a time she died.

units.zh: 太守蕭琛賻焉，表言其狀。
units.en: Prefect Xiao Chen sent gifts and memorialized what had happened.
units.literal: The prefect Xiao Chen gave funeral gifts and memorialized the affair.

units.zh: 有詔旌其門閭。
units.en: The throne honored her household.
units.literal: An edict honored her gate and lane.

units.zh: 沈崇傃
units.en: Shen Chongsu
units.literal: Shen Chongsu

units.zh: 沈崇傃字思整，吳興武康人也。
units.en: Shen Chongsu, styled Si Zheng, was from Wukang in Wuxing.
units.literal: Shen Chongsu, courtesy name Si Zheng, was a man of Wukang in Wuxing.

units.zh: 父懷明，宋兗州刺史。
units.en: His father Huaiming had been Song Inspector of Yanzhou.
units.literal: His father Huaiming had been Inspector of Yanzhou under Song.

units.zh: 崇傃六歲丁父憂，哭踴過禮。
units.en: At six he lost his father and mourned beyond propriety.
units.literal: At six Chongsu suffered his father's death and wept and stamped beyond the rites.

units.zh: 及長，傭書以養母焉。
units.en: Grown, he copied books to feed his mother.
units.literal: When grown he copied books to support his mother.

units.zh: 齊建武初，起家爲奉朝請。
units.en: In early Jianwu he entered service as Attendant at Court.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwu era he first took office as Attendant at Court.

units.zh: 永元末，遷司徒行參軍。
units.en: At Yongyuan's end he became staff aide to the Minister of Education.
units.literal: At the end of the Yongyuan era he was promoted to staff aide in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 天監初，爲前軍鄱陽王參軍事。
units.en: Early in Tianjian he was staff officer to the Forward Army's Prince of Poyang.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Tianjian era he served as staff officer to the Prince of Poyang in the Forward Army.

units.zh: 三年，太守柳惲辟爲主簿。
units.en: In year three Prefect Liu Yun made him chief clerk.
units.literal: In the third year the prefect Liu Yun engaged him as chief clerk.

units.zh: 崇傃從惲到郡，還迎其母，母卒。
units.en: Chongsu went with Yun to the prefecture, then went back for his mother; she died on the way.
units.literal: Chongsu followed Yun to the commandery, then returned to fetch his mother; his mother died.

units.zh: 崇傃以不及侍疾，將欲致死，水漿不入口，晝夜號哭，旬日殆將絕氣。
units.en: Having missed her sickbed, he meant to die: no food or drink, weeping day and night until in ten days he was all but gone.
units.literal: Chongsu, because he had not been able to tend her in her illness, was about to die himself: he would not take water or food and wept day and night; in ten days he was nearly dead.

units.zh: 兄弟謂之曰：「殯葬未申，遽自毀滅，非全孝之道也。」
units.en: His brothers said, "The funeral is not settled—if you kill yourself now, that is not complete filial duty."
units.literal: His brothers said to him: "The burial is not yet arranged—if you destroy yourself in haste, that is not the full way of filial piety."

units.zh: 崇傃之瘞所，不避雨雪，倚墳哀慟。
units.en: He would not leave the grave in rain or snow and leaned on the mound wailing.
units.literal: At the burial ground Chongsu did not avoid rain or snow but leaned on the mound in grief.

units.zh: 每夜恒有猛獸來望之，有聲狀如歎息者。
units.en: Nightly wild beasts came to watch him, sighing as they came.
units.literal: Each night fierce beasts would come to look upon him, with sounds like sighing.

units.zh: 家貧無以遷窆，乃行乞經年，始獲葬焉。
units.en: Too poor to rebury her, he begged a full year before he could lay her to rest.
units.literal: The family was poor and could not move the grave; he begged for a year before he could bury her.

units.zh: 旣而廬於墓側，自以初行喪禮不備，復以葬後更治服三年。
units.en: Then he hutched beside the tomb; thinking the first mourning rites incomplete, he wore mourning again for three years after burial.
units.literal: Thereafter he built a hut beside the tomb; because he felt his first mourning had been incomplete, after the burial he observed mourning dress again for three years.

units.zh: 久食麥屑，不啖鹽酢，坐臥于單薦，因虛腫不能起。
units.en: He lived on bran without salt or vinegar, sat and slept on one thin mat, and swelled so weak he could not stand.
units.literal: For long he ate only wheat bran and would not touch salt or vinegar; he sat and lay on a single mat until, from emaciation, he could not rise.

units.zh: 郡縣舉其至孝。
units.en: Commandery and county commended his extreme filiality.
units.literal: The commandery and county reported his utmost filial piety.

units.zh: 高祖聞，卽遣中書舍人慰勉之，乃下詔曰：「前軍沈崇傃，少有志行，居喪逾禮。
units.en: Gaozu heard and sent a Secretariat Attendant to comfort him, then issued an edict: "Forward Army Shen Chongsu showed resolve young and mourning beyond measure.
units.literal: When Gaozu heard, he at once sent a Secretariat Attendant to comfort and encourage him, and issued an edict saying: "Shen Chongsu of the Forward Army, in youth had resolve and conduct; in mourning he exceeded the rites.

units.zh: 齋制不終，未得大葬，自以行乞淹年，哀典多闕，方欲以永慕之晨，更爲再朞之始。
units.en: His fast was unfinished and the great burial undone; after a year of begging the rites still lacked, and he would begin another mourning cycle from that dawn of grief.
units.literal: His fast was not finished and the great burial had not been performed; he himself felt that a year of begging had left the funeral rites much wanting, and he meant to begin a second mourning term from the morning of everlasting longing.

units.zh: 雖卽情可矜，禮有明斷。
units.en: Pity his heart, but rites have limits.
units.literal: Though feeling may be pitiable, the rites have clear limits.

units.zh: 可便令除釋，擢補太子洗馬。
units.en: Release him from mourning and appoint Crown Prince's Household Steward.
units.literal: Let him at once be released from mourning dress and promoted to fill the post of Crown Prince's Household Steward.

units.zh: 旌彼門閭，敦茲風教。」
units.en: Honor his household and strengthen this custom."
units.literal: Honor his gate and lane and thicken this teaching of custom."

units.zh: 崇傃奉詔釋服，而涕泣如居喪，固辭不受官，苦自陳讓，經年乃得爲永寧令。
units.en: He obeyed and doffed mourning but wept as in bereavement, refused the post, pleaded hard, and only after a year took Yongning magistracy.
units.literal: Chongsu received the edict and put off mourning dress, yet wept as if still in mourning; he firmly refused the office, pleaded bitterly, and only after a year did he become magistrate of Yongning.

units.zh: 自以祿不及養，怛恨愈甚，哀思不自堪，至縣卒，時年三十九。
units.en: His stipend could no longer feed his mother; grief overwhelmed him and he died in office at thirty-nine.
units.literal: He felt that his salary could no longer nourish his mother; regret and grief grew worse, his sorrow unbearable, and at the county he died, aged thirty-nine.

units.zh: 荀匠字文師，潁陰人，晉太保勗九世孫也。
units.en: Xun Jiang, styled Wen Shi, of Yingyin, was ninth generation from Jin Grand Tutor Xun Xu.
units.literal: Xun Jiang, courtesy name Wen Shi, was a man of Yingyin, ninth-generation descendant of Jin Grand Tutor Xun Xu.

units.zh: 祖瓊，年十五，復父仇於成都市，以孝聞。
units.en: His grandfather Qiong at fifteen avenged his father in Chengdu market and won fame for filial piety.
units.literal: His grandfather Qiong, at fifteen, avenged his father's death in Chengdu market and was known for filial piety.

units.zh: 宋元嘉末，渡淮赴武陵王義，爲元凶追兵所殺，贈員外散騎侍郎。
units.en: Late in Song Yuanjia he crossed the Huai for Prince of Wuling Yi, was killed by the crown prince's pursuers, and was posthumously made Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
units.literal: At the end of the Yuanjia era of Song he crossed the Huai to join Prince of Wuling Yi and was killed by the crown prince's pursuing troops; posthumously he was given the title Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.

units.zh: 父法超，齊中興末爲安復令，卒於官。
units.en: His father Fachao, late in Qi Zhongxing, was Anfu magistrate and died in office.
units.literal: His father Fachao, at the end of the Zhongxing era of Qi, was magistrate of Anfu and died in office.

units.zh: 凶問至，匠號慟氣絕，身體皆冷，至夜乃蘇。
units.en: When word came he wailed himself breathless and cold; only at night did he wake.
units.literal: When the dire news arrived Jiang wailed until his breath stopped and his whole body was cold; only at night did he revive.

units.zh: 旣而奔喪，每宿江渚，商旅皆不忍聞其哭聲。
units.en: Rushing to the funeral he lodged nightly on the river sandbars; travelers could not bear his crying.
units.literal: Then he hurried to the mourning; each night he lodged on the river islets, and travelers could not bear to hear his weeping.

units.zh: 服未闋，兄斐起家爲鬰林太守，征俚賊，爲流矢所中，死於陣。
units.en: Mourning unfinished, his brother Fei became Yulin governor, fought the Liao raiders, took a stray arrow, and died on the field.
units.literal: Before mourning was finished his elder brother Fei first took office as governor of Yulin, campaigned against the Liao bandits, was struck by a stray arrow, and died in battle.

units.zh: 喪還，匠迎于豫章，望舟投水，傍人赴救，僅而得全。
units.en: The bier returning, he met it at Yuzhang, saw the boat, and leapt into the river; bystanders barely saved him.
units.literal: When the coffin returned Jiang met it at Yuzhang, saw the boat, and threw himself into the water; those beside him rescued him and he barely survived.

units.zh: 旣至，家貧不得時葬。
units.en: Home again, they were too poor to bury on time.
units.literal: When he arrived, the family was poor and could not bury in season.

units.zh: 居父憂並兄服，歷四年不出廬戶。
units.en: He mourned father and brother together—four years without leaving the mourning hut.
units.literal: He observed mourning for his father together with mourning for his brother—four years without leaving the hut door.

units.zh: 自括發後，不復櫛沐，髮皆禿落。
units.en: From binding his hair he never combed or bathed, and his hair fell out.
units.literal: After he bound up his hair he never combed or washed again, and his hair all fell out.

units.zh: 哭無時，聲盡則係之以泣，目眥皆爛，形體枯顇，皮骨裁連，雖家人不復識。
units.en: He wept without cease; when voice failed he sobbed on; his eyelids rotted, his body skeletal; kin scarcely knew him.
units.literal: He wept without fixed times; when his voice was gone he tied on sobbing, his eyelids all ulcerated, his form withered and gaunt, skin and bone barely joined—even his family no longer knew him.

units.zh: 郡縣以狀言，高祖詔遣中書舍人爲其除服，擢爲豫章王國左常侍。
units.en: Commandery and county reported; Gaozu sent a Secretariat Attendant to release mourning and make him Left Regular Attendant in Prince of Yuzhang's kingdom.
units.literal: The commandery and county reported the facts; Gaozu issued an edict that a Secretariat Attendant should release him from mourning and promote him to Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of the Prince of Yuzhang.

units.zh: 匠雖卽吉，毀顇逾甚。
units.en: Though he left mourning, his wasting grew worse.
units.literal: Though Jiang had returned to the ordinary calendar, his devastation grew worse.

units.zh: 外祖孫謙誡之曰：「主上以孝治天下，汝行過古人，故發明詔，擢汝此職。
units.en: His maternal grandfather Sun Qian warned him: "The throne rules by filial piety; your conduct exceeds the ancients, hence the edict and this appointment.
units.literal: His maternal grandfather Sun Qian admonished him, saying: "The sovereign rules the realm by filial piety; your conduct surpasses the ancients, and therefore the bright edict was issued and you were raised to this post.

units.zh: 非唯君父之命難拒，故亦揚名後世，所顯豈獨汝身哉！」
units.en: You cannot only refuse a lord-father's command—you will win fame for ages; the glory is not yours alone!"
units.literal: It is not only that a lord and father's command is hard to refuse—you will also make a name for later ages; the glory shown is not yours alone!"

units.zh: 匠於是乃拜。
units.en: Then Jiang accepted the post.
units.literal: Thereupon Jiang bowed in acceptance.

units.zh: 竟以毀卒於家，時年二十一。
units.en: He died at home of grief at twenty-one.
units.literal: In the end, from devastation he died at home, aged twenty-one.

units.zh: 庾黔婁
units.en: Yu Qianlou
units.literal: Yu Qianlou

units.zh: 庾黔婁字子貞，新野人也。
units.en: Yu Qianlou, styled Zi Zhen, was from Xinye.
units.literal: Yu Qianlou, courtesy name Zi Zhen, was a man of Xinye.

units.zh: 父易，司徒主簿，徵不至，有高名。
units.en: His father Yi had been Secretariat chief clerk, was summoned but would not serve, and had great repute.
units.literal: His father Yi had been chief clerk in the Secretariat; summoned but he did not come, and he enjoyed a high reputation.

units.zh: 黔婁少好學，多講誦《孝經》，未嘗失色於人，南陽高士劉虬、宗測並歎異之。
units.en: From youth he loved learning, often expounded the Classic of Filial Piety, never lost composure before others; Nanyang worthies Liu Qiu and Zong Ce both admired him.
units.literal: Qianlou from youth loved learning and often lectured on the Classic of Filial Piety; he never changed countenance before others; the eminent men of Nanyang, Liu Qiu and Zong Ce, both marveled at him.

units.zh: 起家本州主簿，遷平西行參軍。
units.en: He began as native-province chief clerk, then became Pacifying West staff aide.
units.literal: His first office was chief clerk in his native province; he was transferred to staff aide in the Pacifying West headquarters.

units.zh: 出爲編令，治有異績。
units.en: As Bian magistrate his rule won unusual praise.
units.literal: He went out as magistrate of Bian and in governing achieved outstanding results.

units.zh: 先是，縣境多虎暴。
units.en: Before, tigers ravaged the county.
units.literal: Before this, within the county boundaries tigers were fierce and violent.

units.zh: 黔婁至，虎皆渡往臨沮界，當時以爲仁化所感。
units.en: When Qianlou came the tigers all crossed into Linju; men said humane rule had moved them.
units.literal: When Qianlou arrived the tigers all crossed to the border of Linju; at the time people took it as the effect of humane transformation.

units.zh: 齊永元初，除孱陵令，到縣未旬，易在家遘疾，黔婁忽然心驚，舉身流汗，卽日棄官歸家，家人悉驚其忽至。
units.en: Early in Qi Yongyuan he became Chanling magistrate; within ten days Yi fell ill at home; Qianlou felt a sudden dread, broke into sweat, and that day quit office and ran home—kin were stunned.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Yongyuan era of Qi he was appointed magistrate of Chanling; he had been at the county less than ten days when Yi fell ill at home; Qianlou suddenly felt alarm in his heart, sweat poured over his whole body, and that same day he abandoned office and returned home; the family was all startled at his sudden arrival.

units.zh: 時易疾始二日，醫云：「欲知差劇，但嘗糞甜苦。」
units.en: Yi had been ill only two days; the doctor said, "To know if he will live or die, taste whether the stool is sweet or bitter."
units.literal: At that time Yi's illness had only begun two days before; the physician said: "To know whether he will improve or worsen, only taste whether the feces are sweet or bitter."

units.zh: 易泄痢，黔婁輒取嘗之，味轉甜滑，心逾憂苦。
units.en: Yi had dysentery; Qianlou tasted it—the flavor grew sweet and smooth, and his grief deepened.
units.literal: Yi had dysentery; Qianlou at once took some and tasted it—the flavor turned sweet and smooth, and his heart grew more bitter with worry.

units.zh: 至夕，每稽顙北辰，求以身代。
units.en: Each night he bowed to the Pole Star, begging to die in his father's stead.
units.literal: Each evening he knocked his forehead to the North Star, begging to take his father's place.

units.zh: 俄聞空中有聲曰：「徵君壽命盡，不復可延，汝誠禱旣至，止得申至月末。」
units.en: Soon a voice in the air said, "The Recluse's span is done and cannot be added; your prayer reached heaven—you may only extend him to month's end."
units.literal: Soon a voice was heard in the air saying: "The Recluse's allotted life is finished and cannot be extended; your prayer has indeed reached us—you may only extend him to the end of the month."

units.zh: 及晦而易亡，黔婁居喪過禮，廬于冢側。
units.en: On the last day Yi died; Qianlou mourned beyond measure and hutched beside the tomb.
units.literal: On the last day of the month Yi died; Qianlou observed mourning beyond the rites and hutted beside the mound.

units.zh: 和帝卽位，將起之，鎮軍蕭穎胄手書敦譬，黔婁固辭。
units.en: When Emperor He acceded they meant to call him; Pacifying Army Xiao Yingzhou wrote urging him, but Qianlou refused firmly.
units.literal: When Emperor He took the throne they were about to summon him; the Pacifying Army Xiao Yingzhou wrote in his own hand urging and instructing him, but Qianlou firmly refused.

units.zh: 服闋，除西臺尚書儀曹郎。
units.en: After mourning he became Western Terrace Gentleman of Ceremonies.
units.literal: When mourning was finished he was appointed Gentleman of Ceremonies in the Western Terrace.

units.zh: 梁臺建，鄧元起爲益州刺史，表黔婁爲府長史、巴西、梓潼二郡太守。
units.en: As Liang was forming Deng Yuanqi became Yizhou inspector and named Qianlou headquarters chief clerk and governor of Baxi and Zitong.
units.literal: When the Liang regime was being established Deng Yuanqi became Inspector of Yizhou and memorialized Qianlou as chief clerk of the headquarters and governor of the two commanderies of Baxi and Zitong.

units.zh: 及成都平，城中珍寶山積，元起悉分與僚佐，惟黔婁一無所取。
units.en: When Chengdu fell treasures heaped in the city; Yuanqi shared them among his staff, but Qianlou took nothing.
units.literal: When Chengdu was pacified treasures in the city piled like mountains; Yuanqi divided them all among his staff, but Qianlou took not a single thing.

units.zh: 元起惡其異衆，厲聲曰：「長史何獨爾爲！」
units.en: Yuanqi hated his singularity and snapped, "Chief Clerk—why alone act so!"
units.literal: Yuanqi resented his standing apart from the crowd and said in a harsh voice: "Chief Clerk—why alone act thus!"

units.zh: 黔婁示不違之，請書數篋。
units.en: Qianlou seemed to comply but asked only for a few baskets of books.
units.literal: Qianlou showed that he did not disobey but asked only for several baskets of books.

units.zh: 尋除蜀郡太守，在職清素，百姓便之。
units.en: Soon he was Shu governor, pure and spare in office, and the people were at ease.
units.literal: Soon after he was appointed governor of Shu commandery; in office he was pure and plain, and the common people found him easy to live under.

units.zh: 元起死于蜀，部曲皆散，黔婁身營殯殮，攜持喪柩歸鄉里。
units.en: Yuanqi died in Shu and his troops dispersed; Qianlou himself arranged the funeral and bore the coffin home.
units.literal: Yuanqi died in Shu; his troops all scattered; Qianlou himself arranged the burial and coffining and carried the bier back to his home district.

units.zh: 還爲尚書金部郎，遷中軍表記室參軍。
units.en: Back he became Secretariat Gentleman of the Golden Department, then Central Army staff recorder.
units.literal: On return he became Gentleman of the Golden Department in the Secretariat and was transferred to staff recorder in the Central Army headquarters.

units.zh: 東宮建，以本官侍皇太子讀，甚見知重，詔與太子中庶子殷鈞、中舍人到洽、國子博士明山賓等，遞日爲太子講《五經》義。
units.en: When the Eastern Palace rose he attended the crown prince in study, won high favor, and by edict he, with Household Mentor Yin Jun, Attendant Dao Qia, Erudite Ming Shanbin, and others, lectured the crown prince daily on the Five Classics.
units.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established he served in his former office attending the Crown Prince in study, was greatly known and esteemed, and by edict he, together with the Crown Prince's Household Mentor Yin Jun, Household Attendant Dao Qia, and National University Erudite Ming Shanbin and others, took turns daily lecturing the Crown Prince on the meaning of the Five Classics.

units.zh: 遷散騎侍郎、荊州大中正。
units.en: He became Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Jingzhou Grand Rectifier.
units.literal: He was transferred to Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Rectifier of Jingzhou.

units.zh: 卒，時年四十六。
units.en: He died at forty-six.
units.literal: He died, aged forty-six.

units.zh: 吉翂字彥霄，馮翊蓮勺人也。
units.en: Ji Bin, styled Yan Xiao, was from Lianzhao in Fengyi.
units.literal: Ji Bin, courtesy name Yan Xiao, was a man of Lianzhao in Fengyi.

units.zh: 世居襄陽。
units.en: The clan had long lived in Xiangyang.
units.literal: For generations the family dwelt in Xiangyang.

units.zh: 翂幼有孝性。
units.en: From childhood Bin was filial.
units.literal: Bin from childhood had a filial nature.

units.zh: 年十一，遭所生母憂，水漿不入口，殆將滅性，親黨異之。
units.en: At eleven he mourned his birth mother, took no food or drink, nearly died of grief, and kin marveled.
units.literal: At eleven he suffered mourning for his birth mother; he would not take water or broth and was nearly destroyed in nature; kin and neighbors marveled at him.

units.zh: 天監初，父爲吳興原鄉令，爲姦吏所誣，逮詣廷尉。
units.en: Early in Tianjian his father was Yuan township magistrate in Wuxing, was framed by a corrupt clerk, and was sent to the Court of Justice.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Tianjian era his father was magistrate of Yuan township in Wuxing and was slandered by a corrupt clerk and seized and sent to the Court of Justice.

units.zh: 翂年十五，號泣衢路，祈請公卿，行人見者，皆爲隕涕。
units.en: Bin at fifteen wailed in the streets, pleading with high officials; every passerby wept.
units.literal: Bin, aged fifteen, wept and wailed in the public streets, begging the high ministers; passersby who saw him all shed tears.

units.zh: 其父理雖清白，恥爲吏訊，乃虛自引咎，罪當大辟。
units.en: Though his father was innocent, he was shamed to be examined as a criminal and falsely confessed; the penalty was death.
units.literal: Though his father's case was in truth innocent, he was ashamed to be questioned as a criminal and therefore falsely confessed guilt himself; the crime called for the great execution.

units.zh: 翂乃撾登聞鼓，乞代父命。
units.en: Bin then struck the petition drum and begged to die for his father.
units.literal: Bin then beat the petition drum at the palace gate and begged to die in his father's place.

units.zh: 高祖異之，敕廷尉卿蔡法度曰：「吉翂請死贖父，義誠可嘉；
units.en: Gaozu was moved and ordered Minister of Justice Cai Fadu: "Ji Bin asks to die for his father—his loyalty is admirable;
units.literal: Gaozu marveled at it and ordered the Minister of Justice Cai Fadu, saying: "Ji Bin asks to die to redeem his father—the righteousness and sincerity are truly admirable;

units.zh: 但其幼童，未必自能造意。
units.en: but he is a child and may not have thought of this himself.
units.literal: but he is still a young child and may not himself have formed the intent.

units.zh: 卿可嚴加脅誘，取其款實。」
units.en: Coerce and entice him strictly and get the full truth."
units.literal: You may strictly coerce and entice him and obtain his full confession."

units.zh: 法度受敕還寺，盛陳徽纏，備列官司，厲色問翂曰：「爾求代父死，敕已相許，便應伏法。
units.en: Fadu took the order, returned to court, spread out chains and fetters, lined up the officials, and sternly asked Bin: "You ask to die for your father—the edict already grants it; you should submit to execution.
units.literal: Fadu received the order and returned to his office; he displayed fetters and chains in profusion, arrayed the officials in full, and with stern countenance questioned Bin, saying: "You ask to die in your father's place—the edict has already granted it, and you ought to submit to the law.

units.zh: 然刀鋸至劇，審能死不？
units.en: But blade and saw are cruel—can you truly die?
units.literal: Yet knife and saw are most severe—can you in truth face death?

units.zh: 且爾童孺，志不及此，必爲人所教。
units.en: You are only a boy; your heart cannot reach here—you were taught by someone.
units.literal: Moreover you are a mere child; your will does not reach to this—you must have been taught by someone.

units.zh: 姓名是誰，可具列答。
units.en: Name him—answer fully.
units.literal: What is his name—give a full list in answer.

units.zh: 若有悔異，亦相聽許。」
units.en: If you repent, we will hear it."
units.literal: If you repent and change your mind, that too will be allowed."

units.zh: 翂對曰：「囚雖蒙弱，豈不知死可畏憚？
units.en: Bin answered: "Though I am weak, do I not know death is fearful?
units.literal: Bin answered: "Though the prisoner is feeble and weak, does he not know that death is to be feared?

units.zh: 顧諸弟稚藐，唯囚爲長，不忍見父極刑，自延視息。
units.en: My brothers are small; I alone am eldest—I cannot watch my father die while I live on.
units.literal: But my younger brothers are young and small; only the prisoner is the eldest—I cannot bear to see my father suffer the extreme penalty and myself prolong my breath.

units.zh: 所以內斷胸臆，上干萬乘。
units.en: So I broke my heart within and troubled the throne above.
units.literal: Therefore I cut off my heart within and troubled the Son of Heaven above.

units.zh: 今欲殉身不測，委骨泉壤，此非細故，奈何受人教邪！
units.en: Now I would throw my body into the unknown and leave my bones underground—this is no small thing; how could another teach me!
units.literal: Now I wish to cast away my body into the unknown and leave my bones in the springs and mounds—this is no small matter; how could I accept another's teaching!

units.zh: 明詔聽代，不異登仙，豈有回貳！」
units.en: The clear edict lets me substitute—it is like ascending to immortality; how could I waver!"
units.literal: The bright edict permits substitution—no different from ascending as an immortal; how could there be second thoughts!"

units.zh: 法度知翂至心有在，不可屈撓，乃更和顏誘語之曰：「主上知尊侯無罪，行當釋亮。
units.en: Fadu saw Bin's heart could not be broken; he softened and said, "The throne knows your father is innocent and will free him soon.
units.literal: Fadu knew Bin's resolve was fixed and could not be bent; he changed to gentle persuasion and said, "The emperor knows your honored father is guiltless and will soon release him.

units.zh: 觀君神儀明秀，足稱佳童，今若轉辭，幸父子同濟。
units.en: You are bright and handsome, a model youth—turn back now and father and son may yet be spared.
units.literal: You look bright and noble—truly a fine youth. If you change your plea now, perhaps father and son may both be saved.

units.zh: 奚以此妙年，苦求湯鑊？」
units.en: Why at this tender age court the boiling cauldron?"
units.literal: Why in the flower of youth do you seek the cauldron and blade so bitterly?"

units.zh: 翂對曰：「凡鯤鮞螻蟻，尚惜其生；
units.en: Bin answered, "Even minnows and ants cling to life;
units.literal: Bin replied, "Even fish fry and ants cherish their lives;

units.zh: 況在人斯，豈願齏粉？
units.en: how much more a man—who would choose to be pulverized?
units.literal: how much more a man—who would wish to be ground to dust?

units.zh: 但囚父掛深劾，必正刑書，故思殞仆，冀延父命。
units.en: But my father faces capital charge; I offer my life to prolong his.
units.literal: Yet my father hangs under grave accusation and must face the full penalty; I mean to throw away my life hoping to extend his.

units.zh: 今瞑目引領，以聽大戮，情殫意極，無言復對。」
units.en: I shut my eyes and await the blade—heart and words are spent; I will not answer again."
units.literal: Now I close my eyes and stretch my neck for the great execution—feeling and will are spent; I have nothing more to say."

units.zh: 翂初見囚，獄掾依法備加桎梏；
units.en: When Bin entered prison the clerks, by statute, fitted him with every bond;
units.literal: When Bin was first imprisoned the jailers, by law, loaded him with full shackles;

units.zh: 法度矜之，命脫其二械，更令著一小者。
units.en: Fadu took pity and had two removed, leaving only a lighter set.
units.literal: Fadu pitied him and ordered two bonds removed, allowing a lighter pair.

units.zh: 翂弗聽，曰：「翂求代父死，死罪之囚，唯宜增益，豈可減乎？」
units.en: Bin refused: "I seek to die for my father—a man under death sentence should wear more, not less?"
units.literal: Bin would not agree and said, "I ask to die for my father—a capital convict should only have bonds added; how may they be lessened?"

units.zh: 竟不脫械。
units.en: and he would not let them be taken off.
units.literal: In the end he would not remove them.

units.zh: 法度具以奏聞，高祖乃宥其父。
units.en: Fadu memorialized all of it; Gaozu then spared his father.
units.literal: Fadu reported everything in full; Gaozu then pardoned his father.

units.zh: 丹陽尹王志求其在廷尉故事，幷請鄉居，欲於歲首，舉充純孝之選。
units.en: Dan'yang magistrate Wang Zhi looked up his file at the Court of Justice and asked his home place too, planning to nominate him for pure filial piety at the new year.
units.literal: Dan'yang magistrate Wang Zhi sought his case in the Court of Justice records and asked his township as well, intending at year's start to recommend him for the pure filial selection.

units.zh: 翂曰：「異哉王尹，何量翂之薄乎！
units.en: Bin said, "Strange, Magistrate Wang—how little you think of Bin!
units.literal: Bin said, "How strange, Magistrate Wang—how shallow you judge Bin!

units.zh: 夫父辱子死，斯道固然。
units.en: When a father is disgraced, a son should die—that is the way.
units.literal: When a father is shamed, a son dies—that is right and proper.

units.zh: 若翂有靦面目，當其此舉，則是因父買名，一何甚辱！」
units.en: Had I any shame left after this, it would mean buying a name at my father's cost—how vile!"
units.literal: If Bin had face to live, having done this act, it would be buying fame through one's father—how shameful!"

units.zh: 拒之而止。
units.en: He declined and would hear no more.
units.literal: He refused and put a stop to it.

units.zh: 年十七，應辟爲本州主簿。
units.en: At seventeen he was summoned as the province's chief clerk.
units.literal: At seventeen he answered summons as chief clerk of his province.

units.zh: 出監萬年縣，攝官朞月，風化大行。
units.en: He supervised Wannian county; in one month as acting magistrate custom was greatly reformed.
units.literal: He went out to supervise Wannian county; as acting magistrate for one cycle customs were greatly transformed.

units.zh: 自雍還至郢，湘州刺史柳悅復召爲主簿。
units.en: From Yong he came back to Ying; Liu Yue, inspector of Xiangzhou, again made him chief clerk.
units.literal: From Yong he returned to Ying; Xiangzhou inspector Liu Yue again summoned him as chief clerk.

units.zh: 後鄉人裴儉、丹陽尹丞臧盾、揚州中正張仄連名薦翂，以爲孝行純至，明通《易》、《老》。
units.en: Later Pei Jian of his town, Zang Dun of Dan'yang, and Zhang Ze, Yangzhou rectifier, jointly praised Bin's pure filiality and clear grasp of the Changes and Laozi.
units.literal: Later townsman Pei Jian, Dan'yang assistant magistrate Zang Dun, and Yangzhou rectifier Zhang Ze jointly recommended Bin, finding his filial conduct pure and his mastery of the Changes and Laozi clear.

units.zh: 敕付太常旌舉。
units.en: An edict sent the matter to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices for public commendation.
units.literal: An edict ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to proclaim and recommend him.

units.zh: 初，翂以父陷罪，因成悸疾，後因發而卒。
units.en: From his father's ordeal he had taken a trembling sickness; later he died when it broke out.
units.literal: Earlier, because his father fell into guilt, he developed a trembling illness; later he died when it flared.

units.zh: 甄恬字彥約，中山無極人也，世居江陵。
units.en: Zhen Tian, styled Yanyue, came from Wuji in Zhongshan; his family had dwelt in Jiangling for generations.
units.literal: Zhen Tian, styled Yanyue, was a man of Wuji in Zhongshan; his clan had long lived in Jiangling.

units.zh: 祖欽之，長寧令。
units.en: His grandfather Qinzhi was magistrate of Changning.
units.literal: His grandfather Qinzhi had been magistrate of Changning.

units.zh: 父標之，州從事。
units.en: His father Biaozhi was a provincial adjutant.
units.literal: His father Biaozhi had been a provincial adjutant.

units.zh: 恬數歲喪父，哀感有若成人。
units.en: Tian lost his father as a small child, mourning like a grown man.
units.literal: Tian lost his father at several years old, grief like an adult's.

units.zh: 家人矜其小，以肉汁和飯飼之，恬不肯食。
units.en: Kin, pitying his age, mixed broth into his rice; Tian refused it.
units.literal: The family pitied his youth and fed him rice mixed with broth; Tian would not eat.

units.zh: 年八歲，問其母，恨生不識父，遂悲泣累日，忽若有見，言其形貌，則其父也，時以爲孝感。
units.en: At eight he told his mother he hated never knowing his father, wept for days, then seemed to see someone and described his looks—it was his father; men called it filial portent.
units.literal: At eight he asked his mother, grieving he had never known his father; he wept for days until suddenly he seemed to see one and spoke his features—it was his father; at the time this was deemed filial response.

units.zh: 家貧，養母常得珍羞。
units.en: Poor as they were, he always found fine food for his mother.
units.literal: Though the household was poor, in nurturing his mother he always obtained delicacies.

units.zh: 及居喪，廬於墓側，恒有鳥玄黃雜色，集於廬樹，恬哭則鳴，哭止則止。
units.en: Mourning at the grave he built a hut; black-and-yellow birds always perched on its tree—when Tian wept they called, when he ceased they ceased.
units.literal: In mourning he hutted by the tomb; constantly birds of mixed black and yellow gathered on the hut tree—when Tian wept they cried, when he stopped they stopped.

units.zh: 又有白雀栖宿其廬。
units.en: A white sparrow roosted on the hut as well.
units.literal: A white sparrow also roosted on his hut.

units.zh: 州將始興王憺表其行狀。
units.en: Xiao Dan, Prince of Shixing and provincial commander, reported his conduct.
units.literal: The provincial commander, Prince of Shixing Xiao Dan, memorialized his conduct.

units.zh: 詔曰：「朕虛己欽賢，寤寐盈想。
units.en: The edict read, "We humble ourselves before the worthy and think of them waking and sleeping.
units.literal: Edict said, "We empty ourselves to honor the worthy, longing day and night.

units.zh: 詔彼群岳，務盡搜揚。
units.en: We command the high officials to seek and raise them without fail.
units.literal: We charge the mountain peaks to search and lift all they can.

units.zh: 恬旣孝行殊異，聲著邦壤，敦風厲俗，弘益茲多。
units.en: Tian's filiality is extraordinary, his name known in every district—he steels the folk and brings great good.
units.literal: Tian's filial conduct is truly rare, his fame filling the land—he ennobles custom and profits the realm greatly.

units.zh: 牧守騰聞，義同親覽。
units.en: The governors have sent word; We receive it as if with Our own eyes.
units.literal: The shepherds and guards have reported up; it is as if We read it ourselves.

units.zh: 可旌表室閭，加以爵位。」
units.en: Let his gate and lane be honored and rank be granted."
units.literal: He may be marked at his gate and lane and given rank."

units.zh: 恬官至安南行參軍。
units.en: Tian rose to acting staff officer on the Pacifying South staff.
units.literal: Tian reached the post of acting staff officer on the Pacifying South campaign.

units.zh: 韓懷明
units.en: Han Huaiming
units.literal: Han Huaiming

units.zh: 韓懷明，上黨人也，客居荊州。
units.en: Han Huaiming was from Shangdang and lived as a guest in Jingzhou.
units.literal: Han Huaiming was a man of Shangdang who resided as a guest in Jingzhou.

units.zh: 年十歲，母患屍疰，每發輒危殆。
units.en: At ten his mother had corpse-consumption sickness; every bout nearly took her life.
units.literal: At ten his mother suffered corpse-consumption malady; each attack nearly killed her.

units.zh: 懷明夜於星下稽顙祈禱，時寒甚切，忽聞香氣，空中有人語曰：「童子母須臾永差，無勞自苦。」
units.en: Huaiming knelt under the stars in bitter cold; suddenly fragrance came and a voice above said, "The boy's mother will soon be wholly well—do not torture yourself."
units.literal: Huaiming knelt and prayed under the stars; the cold was piercing—suddenly he smelled fragrance and a voice in the air said, "Your mother's illness will soon be cured for good—do not torment yourself."

units.zh: 未曉，而母豁然平復。
units.en: Before daybreak his mother was completely healed.
units.literal: Before dawn his mother was wholly restored.

units.zh: 鄉里異之。
units.en: Neighbors were astonished.
units.literal: The countryside marveled.

units.zh: 十五喪父，幾至滅性，負土成墳，贈助無所受。
units.en: At fifteen his father died; he nearly perished from grief, piled the grave himself, and took no aid offered.
units.literal: At fifteen he lost his father, nearly wasting away; he carried earth for the mound and accepted no gifts of help.

units.zh: 免喪，與鄉人郭瑀俱師事南陽劉虬。
units.en: After mourning he and Guo Yu of his town studied with Liu Qiu of Nanyang.
units.literal: When mourning ended he and townsman Guo Yu both studied under Liu Qiu of Nanyang.

units.zh: 虬嘗一日廢講，獨居涕泣。
units.en: Once Qiu canceled class for a day and wept by himself.
units.literal: Once Qiu suspended lecture for a day and wept alone.

units.zh: 懷明竊問其故，虬家人答云：「是外祖亡日。」
units.en: Huaiming asked the reason in private; the household said, "It is the day his mother's father died."
units.literal: Huaiming quietly asked why; Qiu's household answered, "It is his maternal grandfather's death-day."

units.zh: 時虬母亦亡矣。
units.en: His own mother was already gone as well.
units.literal: By then Qiu's mother was also dead.

units.zh: 懷明聞之，卽日罷學，還家就養。
units.en: Hearing this, Huaiming quit school the same day and went home to tend her.
units.literal: Huaiming heard and that day left study to return home and serve.

units.zh: 虬歎曰：「韓生無虞丘之恨矣。」
units.en: Qiu sighed, "Han need not bear Yu Qiu's remorse."
units.literal: Qiu sighed, "Master Han need have no regret like Yu Qiu's."

units.zh: 家貧，常肆力以供甘脆，嬉怡膝下，朝夕不離母側。
units.en: The house was poor; he toiled for dainties, merry at her knee, never leaving her side dawn to dusk.
units.literal: Poor at home, he often hired out labor for sweet and tender foods, delighting under his mother's knees, never leaving her day or night.

units.zh: 母年九十一，以壽終，懷明水漿不入口一旬，號哭不絕聲。
units.en: His mother died at ninety-one; Huaiming took no food or drink for ten days and wailed without stopping.
units.literal: His mother died at ninety-one of old age; Huaiming took neither food nor drink for ten days, wailing without cease.

units.zh: 有雙白鳩巢其廬上，字乳馴狎，若家禽焉，服釋乃去。
units.en: Two white doves nested on his hut, rearing young as tame as poultry; they left only when mourning was done.
units.literal: A pair of white doves nested on his mourning hut, feeding their young tamely like barn birds; only when mourning ended did they leave.

units.zh: 旣除喪，蔬食終身，衣衾無改。
units.en: After mourning he ate only vegetables for life and never changed his clothes.
units.literal: After mourning he ate vegetables all his life and never changed his garments.

units.zh: 天監初，刺史始興王憺表言之。
units.en: At the start of Tianjian, Xiao Dan, Prince of Shixing and inspector, reported him.
units.literal: Early in Tianjian the inspector, Prince of Shixing Xiao Dan, memorialized him.

units.zh: 州累辟不就，卒于家。
units.en: The province called him many times; he would not go, and died at home.
units.literal: The province repeatedly summoned him but he would not accept; he died at home.

units.zh: 劉曇淨
units.en: Liu Tanjing
units.literal: Liu Tanjing

units.zh: 劉曇淨字元光，彭城呂人也。
units.en: Liu Tanjing, styled Yuanguang, was from Lyu in Pengcheng.
units.literal: Liu Tanjing, styled Yuanguang, was a man of Lyu in Pengcheng.

units.zh: 祖元真，淮南太守，居郡得罪；
units.en: His grandfather Yuanzhen was governor of Huainan and committed an offense in the commandery;
units.literal: His grandfather Yuanzhen had been Huainan governor and offended while in office;

units.zh: 父慧鏡，歷詣朝士乞哀，懇惻甚至，遂以孝聞。
units.en: his father Huijing went again and again to court notables pleading mercy, utterly earnest, and won fame for filial piety.
units.literal: his father Huijing went repeatedly to court officials begging pity, sincere to the utmost, and became known for filial piety.

units.zh: 曇淨篤行有父風。
units.en: Tanjing's devoted ways matched his father's.
units.literal: Tanjing's steadfast conduct had his father's spirit.

units.zh: 解褐安成王國左常侍。
units.en: He first served as left palace attendant in the Kingdom of Ancheng.
units.literal: On first office he was left palace attendant of the Kingdom of Ancheng.

units.zh: 父卒於郡，曇淨奔喪，不食飲者累日，絕而又蘇。
units.en: His father died in office; Tanjing ran to the funeral and for days took no food or drink, fainting and waking.
units.literal: His father died in the prefecture; Tanjing rushed to mourning and for days ate and drank nothing, dying and reviving.

units.zh: 每哭輒嘔血。
units.en: Every bout of weeping brought up blood.
units.literal: Each time he wept he vomited blood.

units.zh: 服闋，因毀瘠成疾。
units.en: After mourning he sickened from grief-wasting.
units.literal: When mourning ended he fell ill from wasting grief.

units.zh: 會有詔，士姓各舉四科，曇淨叔父慧斐舉以應孝行，高祖用爲海寧令。
units.en: When an edict bade each clan recommend four kinds of men, his uncle Huifei nominated him for filial conduct and Gaozu appointed him Haining magistrate.
units.literal: An edict came for gentry and commoners each to recommend four categories; his uncle Huifei recommended him for filial conduct and Gaozu made him Haining magistrate.

units.zh: 曇淨以兄未爲縣，因以讓兄，乃除安西行參軍。
units.en: His elder brother had no county post yet, so Tanjing yielded the magistracy and was made staff officer on the Pacifying West staff.
units.literal: Tanjing's elder brother had not yet held a county post, so he yielded; he was then made staff officer of the Pacifying West campaign.

units.zh: 父亡後，事母尤淳至，身營飧粥，不以委人。
units.en: After his father died he served his mother with deepest devotion, cooking gruel himself and trusting no one else.
units.literal: After his father's death he served his mother with utmost purity, cooking porridge himself and entrusting it to none.

units.zh: 母疾，衣不解帶。
units.en: When she was ill he never loosened his belt.
units.literal: When his mother fell ill he did not unfasten his belt.

units.zh: 及母亡，水漿不入口者殆一旬。
units.en: When she died he took no food or drink for nearly ten days.
units.literal: When she died he nearly ten days took no food or drink.

units.zh: 母喪權瘞藥王寺。
units.en: His mother was provisionally buried at Medicine King Temple.
units.literal: His mother's coffin was temporarily interred at Medicine King Temple.

units.zh: 時天寒，曇淨身衣單布，廬於瘞所，晝夜哭泣不絕聲，哀感行路，未及朞而卒。
units.en: It was bitter cold; Tanjing wore a single layer, hutted at the grave, weeping day and night—passersby wept; before the year ended he died.
units.literal: The weather was cold; Tanjing wore only thin cloth, hutted at the burial place, weeping day and night without pause—travelers were moved; before the year was out he died.

units.zh: 何炯字士光，廬江灊人也。
units.en: He Jiong, styled Shiguang, was from Qian in Lujiang.
units.literal: He Jiong, styled Shiguang, was a man of Qian in Lujiang.

units.zh: 父撙，太中大夫。
units.en: His father Zun was Grand Master of Palace Counsel.
units.literal: His father Zun was Grand Master of Palace Counsel.

units.zh: 炯年十五，從兄胤受業，一朞並通《五經》章句。
units.en: At fifteen he studied with his cousin Yin; in one year he knew every chapter of the Five Classics.
units.literal: At fifteen Jiong studied with his older cousin Yin; in one cycle he mastered all Five Classics' chapter-and-verse.

units.zh: 炯白皙，美容貌，從兄求、點每稱之曰：「叔寶神清，弘治膚清。
units.en: Pale and handsome, his cousins Qiu and Dian would say, "Shubao's spirit was pure, Hongzhi's complexion pure.
units.literal: Fair and handsome, his cousins Qiu and Dian often praised him: "Shubao's spirit is clear, Hongzhi's skin is clear.

units.zh: 今觀此子，復見衛、杜在目。」
units.en: Now this lad brings Wei and Du back before us."
units.literal: Seeing this boy again, Wei and Du are before our eyes."

units.zh: 炯常慕恬退，不樂進仕。
units.en: Jiong loved simplicity and disliked climbing office.
units.literal: Jiong often admired quiet withdrawal and took no joy in advancement.

units.zh: 從叔昌珝謂曰：「求、點皆已高蹈，爾無宜復爾。
units.en: His uncle Chang Xu told him, "Qiu and Dian have both gone aloft—you need not follow.
units.literal: His uncle Chang Xu said, "Qiu and Dian have both ascended high—you need not do likewise.

units.zh: 且君子出處，亦各一途。」
units.en: A gentleman's rise and retirement are each a proper way."
units.literal: Moreover the gentleman's going forth and staying have each their path."

units.zh: 年十九，解褐揚州主簿。
units.en: At nineteen he entered office as Yangzhou chief clerk.
units.literal: At nineteen he first took office as Yangzhou chief clerk.

units.zh: 舉秀才，累遷王府行參軍、尚書兵、庫部二曹郎。
units.en: Made a cultivated talent, he rose to prince's staff officer and both Military and Treasury bureaus of the Masters of Writing.
units.literal: Recommended as cultivated talent, he rose through prince's staff officer, and both Military and Treasury sections of the Masters of Writing.

units.zh: 出爲永康令，以和理稱。
units.en: He went out as Yongkang magistrate, praised for gentle rule.
units.literal: Sent out as Yongkang magistrate, famed for harmony and order.

units.zh: 還爲仁威南康王限內記室，遷治書侍御史。
units.en: Back as recorder to Prince Renwei of Nankang, then impeachment censor.
units.literal: Returned as recorder within the Prince of Nankang Renwei's domain, then impeachment censor.

units.zh: 以父疾經旬，衣不解帶，頭不櫛沐，信宿之間，形貌頓改。
units.en: His father was sick ten days; Jiong never loosened his belt or washed his hair—in two nights his face was altered.
units.literal: His father was ill for ten days; Jiong did not unfasten his belt or comb or wash—within two nights his form was suddenly changed.

units.zh: 及父卒，號慟不絕聲，枕凷藉地，腰虛腳腫，竟以毀卒。
units.en: When his father died he wailed endlessly, pillow cast aside, waist hollow and legs swollen—he died of grief.
units.literal: When his father died he wailed without cease, his pillow fallen to the ground—his waist failed and legs swelled; he died at last of grief.

units.zh: 庾沙彌
units.en: Yu Shamí
units.literal: Yu Shamí

units.zh: 庾沙彌，潁陰人也。
units.en: Yu Shamí was from Yingyin.
units.literal: Yu Shamí was a man of Yingyin.

units.zh: 晉司空冰六世孫。
units.en: He was sixth in descent from Jin Minister of Works Bing.
units.literal: He was sixth-generation descendant of Jin Minister of Works Bing.

units.zh: 父佩玉，輔國長史、長沙內史，宋昇明中坐沈攸之事誅，沙彌時始生。
units.en: His father Peiyu was chief aide to the Pacifying-the-State general and Changsha administrator; in Song Shengming he was killed in Shen Youzhi's rebellion—Shamí was a newborn.
units.literal: His father Peiyu had been Pacifying the State chief aide and Changsha administrator; in Song's Shengming he was executed for Shen Youzhi's affair—Shamí had just been born.

units.zh: 年至五歲，所生母爲制采衣，輒不肯服。
units.en: At five his birth mother made him bright clothes; he refused to put them on.
units.literal: At five his birth mother had a colored garment made for him; he would not wear it.

units.zh: 母問其故，流涕對曰：「家門禍酷，用是何爲！」
units.en: Asked the reason, he wept and said, "Our clan suffered bitter ruin—what is this for?"
units.literal: When she asked why, he wept and said, "Our house met cruel disaster—of what use is this?"

units.zh: 旣長，終身布衣蔬食。
units.en: Grown, he wore coarse cloth and ate vegetables for life.
units.literal: Grown, he wore plain cloth and ate vegetables all his life.

units.zh: 起家臨川王國左常侍，遷中軍田曹行參軍。
units.en: He started as left palace attendant in the Kingdom of Linchuan, then field-accounts staff officer of the Central Army.
units.literal: He began as left palace attendant of the Kingdom of Linchuan and became acting field-accounts staff officer of the Central Army.

units.zh: 嫡母劉氏寢疾，沙彌晨昏侍側，衣不解帶，或應針灸，輒以身先試之。
units.en: When his stepmother Lady Liu was sick Shamí waited dawn and dusk, belt never loosened; if needles were used he tested them on himself first.
units.literal: When his stepmother Lady Liu lay ill Shamí attended morning and evening, belt unfastened; if acupuncture was needed he tried it on himself first.

units.zh: 及母亡，水漿不入口累日，終喪不解衰絰，不出廬戶，晝夜號慟，鄰人不忍聞。
units.en: When she died he fasted for days, never left his mourning garb or hut, wailing day and night till neighbors could not listen.
units.literal: When she died he took no food or drink for days, through the whole mourning never removing his hemp, never leaving the hut, wailing day and night—neighbors could not bear to hear.

units.zh: 墓在新林，因有旅松百餘株，自生墳側。
units.en: The grave was at Xinlin; over a hundred pines grew by themselves beside the tomb.
units.literal: The tomb was at Xinlin; more than a hundred traveler pines sprang up on their own beside the mound.

units.zh: 族兄都官尚書詠表言其狀，應純孝之舉，高祖召見嘉之，以補歙令。
units.en: His kinsman Yu Yong, Minister President of Justice, reported him for pure filial piety; Gaozu received him, praised him, and made him magistrate of She.
units.literal: His clan elder, Minister President of Justice Yong, memorialized his case for the pure filial recommendation; Gaozu summoned and praised him and appointed him She magistrate.

units.zh: 還除輕車邵陵王參軍事，隨府會稽，復丁所生母憂。
units.en: He returned to office as staff equal to the Prince of Shaoling of Light Chariots, followed the headquarters to Kuaiji, and again mourned his birth mother.
units.literal: He was transferred back and made staff equal on the staff of the Prince of Shaoling, Light Chariots; he followed the prince's headquarters to Kuaiji and again entered mourning for his birth mother.

units.zh: 喪還都，濟浙江，中流遇風，舫將覆沒，沙彌抱柩號哭，俄而風靜，蓋孝感所致。
units.en: On the homeward crossing of the Zhe the boat nearly capsized in a squall; Shami clung to the coffin and wailed, and soon the wind died—men took it as filial feeling answered from Heaven.
units.literal: Returning from mourning to the capital, he crossed the Zhe River; midstream he met wind and the boat was about to capsize—Shami embraced the coffin and wailed, and presently the wind fell still—thought to be moved by filial response.

units.zh: 服闋，除信威刑獄參軍，兼丹陽郡囗囗囗累遷寧遠錄事參軍，轉司馬。
units.en: After mourning he became Trustworthy Might criminal judge staff equal and concurrently [text lost] in Danyang; he rose to Ningyuan recording secretary, then marshal.
units.literal: When mourning ended he was made staff equal of Trustworthy Might criminal judge, concurrently [lacuna] of Danyang commandery; he was promoted in succession recording secretary of Ningyuan and transferred to marshal.

units.zh: 出爲長城令，卒。
units.en: He served as magistrate of Changcheng and died in office.
units.literal: He went out as magistrate of Changcheng and died.

units.zh: 江紑字含潔，濟陽考城人也。
units.en: Jiang Fou, styled Hanjie, was from Kaocheng in Jiyang.
units.literal: Jiang Fou, styled Hanjie, was a man of Kaocheng in Jiyang.

units.zh: 父蒨，光祿大夫。
units.en: His father Qian was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
units.literal: His father Qian was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

units.zh: 紑幼有孝性。
units.en: Gou was filial from childhood.
units.literal: From childhood Gou had a filial nature.

units.zh: 年十三，父患眼，紑侍疾將朞月，衣不解帶。
units.en: At thirteen, when his father had eye trouble, Gou nursed him nearly a month without leaving his side.
units.literal: At thirteen his father suffered eye disease; Gou attended the illness for nearly a month without undoing his belt.

units.zh: 夜夢一僧云：「患眼者，飲慧眼水必差。」
units.en: In a dream a monk told him, "For eye disease, drink Wisdom-Eye water and it will heal."
units.literal: One night he dreamed a monk said, "For eye disease, drink Wisdom-Eye water and you will be cured."

units.zh: 及覺說之，莫能解者。
units.en: He told the dream at dawn, but no one could explain it.
units.literal: When he woke and told it, no one could explain it.

units.zh: 紑第三叔祿與草堂寺智者法師善，往訪之。
units.en: His third uncle Lu was close to the Wise One of Caotang Temple and went to ask him.
units.literal: Gou's third uncle Lu was on good terms with the Wise One of Caotang Temple; he went to visit him.

units.zh: 智者曰：「《無量壽經》云：慧眼見真，能渡彼岸。」
units.en: The Wise One said, "The Infinite Life Sutra says, 'The wisdom-eye sees truth and can ferry to the farther shore.'"
units.literal: The Wise One said, "The Infinite Life Sutra says: the wisdom-eye sees truth and can ferry to the farther shore."

units.zh: 蒨乃因智者啓捨同夏縣界牛屯里舍爲寺，乞賜嘉名。
units.en: Qian then asked the Wise One to petition donating the Niutun estate in Tongxia as a monastery and to grant it a worthy name.
units.literal: Qian thereupon through the Wise One petitioned to donate the house and land at Niutun in Tongxia county as a monastery and begged a fine name.

units.zh: 敕答云：「純臣孝子，往往感應。
units.en: The reply edict said, "Pure ministers and filial sons often meet with response.
units.literal: The edict in reply said, "Pure ministers and filial sons often meet with response.

units.zh: 晉世顏含，遂見冥中送藥。
units.en: In Jin times Yan Han likewise saw medicine sent from the shades.
units.literal: In Jin times Yan Han thus saw medicine sent from the shades.

units.zh: 近見智者，知卿第二息感夢，云飲慧眼水。
units.en: Recently the Wise One told me your second son dreamed of drinking wisdom-eye water.
units.literal: Recently seeing the Wise One, I know your second son was moved in a dream, saying to drink wisdom-eye water.

units.zh: 慧眼則是五眼之一號，若欲造寺，可以慧眼爲名。」
units.en: Wisdom-eye is one of the five eyes; if you build a monastery, call it Wisdom-Eye."
units.literal: Wisdom-eye is the name of one of the five eyes; if you wish to build a monastery, you may take Wisdom-Eye as its name."

units.zh: 及就創造，泄故井，井水清冽，異於常泉。
units.en: When they built, they cleared an old well whose water was clear and sweet, unlike ordinary springs.
units.literal: When construction was undertaken they opened an old well; the well water was clear and sweet, unlike ordinary springs.

units.zh: 依夢取水洗眼及煮藥，稍覺有瘳，因此遂差。
units.en: As the dream directed they washed his eyes and boiled medicine in it; he improved and was cured.
units.literal: Following the dream they took the water to wash the eyes and boil medicine; he felt somewhat better, and thereby was cured.

units.zh: 時人謂之孝感。
units.en: People called it filial feeling answered.
units.literal: Men of the time called it filial feeling answered.

units.zh: 南康王爲南州，召爲迎主簿。
units.en: When the Prince of Nankang governed the south he made Gou reception chief clerk.
units.literal: When the Prince of Nankang was southern inspector he summoned Gou as reception chief clerk.

units.zh: 紑性靜，好《老》、《莊》玄言，尤善佛義，不樂進仕。
units.en: Quiet by nature, he loved Laozi and Zhuangzi and Buddhist teaching and did not care to advance in office.
units.literal: Gou's nature was quiet; he loved the dark learning of Laozi and Zhuangzi and was especially skilled in Buddhist meaning, and did not delight in advancing in office.

units.zh: 及父卒，紑廬于墓，終日號慟不絕聲，月餘卒。
units.en: When his father died he lodged at the tomb and wailed without cease; after more than a month he died.
units.literal: When his father died Gou built a hut at the tomb and wailed without cease all day; after more than a month he died.

units.zh: 劉霽字士烜，平原人也。
units.en: Liu Ji, styled Shixuan, was from Pingyuan.
units.literal: Liu Ji, styled Shixuan, was a man of Pingyuan.

units.zh: 祖乘民，宋冀州刺史。
units.en: His grandfather Chenmin was Song inspector of Ji.
units.literal: His grandfather Chenmin was Song inspector of Ji.

units.zh: 父聞慰，齊工員郎。
units.en: His father Wenwei was a Qi artisan officer.
units.literal: His father Wenwei was a Qi artisan officer.

units.zh: 霽年九歲，能誦《左氏傳》，宗黨咸異之。
units.en: At nine he could recite the Zuo Commentary; kin and clan marveled.
units.literal: At nine years Ji could recite the Zuo Commentary; clan and kin all marveled at him.

units.zh: 十四居父憂，有至性，每哭輒嘔血。
units.en: At fourteen, mourning his father, he was utterly devoted; each cry brought up blood.
units.literal: At fourteen, in mourning for his father, he had utmost nature; each time he wept he vomited blood.

units.zh: 家貧，與弟杳、高槠相篤勵學。
units.en: Poor at home, he and his brothers Xiao and Gao Chu urged one another in study.
units.literal: The family was poor; with his younger brothers Xiao and Gao Chu he urged one another in study.

units.zh: 旣長，博涉多通。
units.en: Grown, he read widely and mastered many subjects.
units.literal: When grown he read widely and mastered many subjects.

units.zh: 天監中，起家奉朝請，稍遷宣惠晉安王府參軍，兼限內記室，出補西昌相。
units.en: In Tianjian he began as court gentleman for attendance, rose to staff equal on the Xuanhui staff of the Prince of Jin'an with concurrent inner-recorder duties, then went out as magistrate of Xichang.
units.literal: In the Tianjian era he first entered office as court gentleman for attendance, then was promoted staff equal on the Xuanhui staff of the Prince of Jin'an, concurrently inner recorder within limits, and went out to fill the post of magistrate of Xichang.

units.zh: 入爲尚書主客侍郎。
units.en: He entered the Secretariat as Master of Guests.
units.literal: He entered office as Master of Guests in the Secretariat.

units.zh: 未朞，除海鹽令。
units.en: Before long he was made magistrate of Haiyan.
units.literal: Before the term ended he was made magistrate of Haiyan.

units.zh: 霽前後宰二邑，並以和理著稱。
units.en: He governed two districts in turn and in both was famed for harmony.
units.literal: Ji in succession governed two districts and in both was famed for harmony and good order.

units.zh: 還爲建康正，非所好。
units.en: He became rectifier of Jiankang, which he did not enjoy.
units.literal: He returned and became rectifier of Jiankang—not to his liking.

units.zh: 頃之，以疾免。
units.en: Soon illness freed him from office.
units.literal: Before long, on illness, he was dismissed.

units.zh: 尋除建康令，不拜。
units.en: He was offered Jiankang again and refused.
units.literal: Shortly after he was made magistrate of Jiankang but would not accept.

units.zh: 母明氏寢疾，霽年已五十，衣不解帶者七旬，誦《觀世音經》，數至萬遍，夜因感夢，見一僧謂曰：「夫人算盡，君精誠篤至，當相爲申延。」
units.en: When his mother Lady Ming fell ill, though fifty he did not leave her side for seventy days, chanting the Guanshiyin sutra tens of thousands of times; in a dream a monk said, "Your mother's span is done, but your devotion is so deep I shall ask to extend it."
units.literal: His mother Lady Ming lay ill; Ji was already fifty and for seventy days did not undo his belt, reciting the Scripture of Guanshiyin Bodhisattva tens of thousands of times; one night, moved in a dream, he saw a monk who said, "Your lady mother's allotted span is ended; your sincerity is utmost—I shall plead to extend it for you."

units.zh: 後六十餘日乃亡。
units.en: She lived more than sixty days longer, then died.
units.literal: After more than sixty days she died.

units.zh: 霽廬于墓，哀慟過禮。
units.en: He lodged at the tomb and mourned beyond the rites.
units.literal: Ji lodged at the tomb and mourned beyond the rites.

units.zh: 常有雙白鶴馴翔廬側。
units.en: A pair of white cranes hovered tame beside his mourning hut.
units.literal: A pair of white cranes constantly hovered tame beside the hut.

units.zh: 處士阮孝緒致書抑譬，霽思慕不已，服未終而卒，時年五十二。
units.en: Ruan Xiaoxu wrote to restrain him, but Ji's longing never ceased; before mourning ended he died at fifty-two.
units.literal: The recluse Ruan Xiaoxu sent a letter to restrain and comfort him, but Ji's longing did not cease; before mourning ended he died, aged fifty-two.

units.zh: 著《釋俗語》八卷，文集十卷。
units.en: He wrote Clarifying Common Speech in eight scrolls and collected works in ten.
units.literal: He authored Clarifying Common Speech in eight scrolls and a collection of writings in ten scrolls.

units.zh: 弟杳在《文學傳》，歊在《處士傳》。
units.en: His brother Xiao has a biography in the Literary Treatise; Gao in the Recluses Treatise.
units.literal: His younger brother Xiao is in the Literary Treatise; Gao is in the Recluses Treatise.

units.zh: 褚脩，吳郡錢唐人也。
units.en: Chu Xiu was from Qiantang in Wu commandery.
units.literal: Chu Xiu was a man of Qiantang in Wu commandery.

units.zh: 父仲都，善《周易》，爲當時最。
units.en: His father Zhongdu mastered the Book of Changes and was foremost of his day.
units.literal: His father Zhongdu was skilled in the Book of Changes and was foremost of his day.

units.zh: 天監中，歷官《五經》博士。
units.en: Under Tianjian he rose to erudite of the Five Classics.
units.literal: In the Tianjian era he held office through the ranks as erudite of the Five Classics.

units.zh: 脩少傳父業，兼通《孝經》、《論語》，善尺牘，頗解文章。
units.en: From youth Xiu took his father's learning, also mastered the Filial Classic and Analects, wrote well, and understood composition.
units.literal: Xiu from youth transmitted his father's craft, and also mastered the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, was skilled at letters, and understood composition fairly well.

units.zh: 初爲湘東王國侍郎，稍遷輕車湘東府行參軍，並兼國子助教。
units.en: He began as gentleman of the Prince of Xiangdong's kingdom, then staff equal on his Light Chariots staff and National University assistant teacher.
units.literal: He first became gentleman of the Prince of Xiangdong's kingdom, then was promoted staff equal on the Light Chariots staff of the Prince of Xiangdong, and concurrently assistant teacher of the National University.

units.zh: 武陵王爲揚州，引爲宣惠參軍、限內記室。
units.en: When the Prince of Wuling governed Yangzhou he made him Xuanhui staff equal and inner recorder.
units.literal: When the Prince of Wuling was Yangzhou inspector he summoned him as staff equal of Xuanhui and inner recorder within limits.

units.zh: 脩性至孝，父喪毀瘠過禮，因患冷氣。
units.en: Utterly filial, he wasted away beyond the rites mourning his father and took a chill in the vital breath.
units.literal: Xiu's nature was utmost filial; in mourning for his father he wasted away beyond the rites and thereby suffered a chill in the vital breath.

units.zh: 及丁母憂，水漿不入口二十三日，氣絕復蘇，每號慟嘔血，遂以毀卒。
units.en: Mourning his mother he took no food for twenty-three days, fainted and revived, wailed until he vomited blood, and died of grief.
units.literal: When he entered mourning for his mother he did not take water or gruel for twenty-three days, lost breath and revived; each time he wailed he vomited blood, and thereby died of grief.

units.zh: 謝藺字希如，陳郡陽夏人也。
units.en: Xie Lan, styled Xiru, was from Yangxia in Chen commandery.
units.literal: Xie Lan, styled Xiru, was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery.

units.zh: 晉太傅安八世孫。
units.en: He was eighth-generation descendant of Jin Grand Tutor An.
units.literal: He was eighth-generation descendant of Jin Grand Tutor An.

units.zh: 父經，中郎諮議參軍。
units.en: His father Jing was staff equal for consultation in the Central Guard.
units.literal: His father Jing was staff equal for consultation in the Central Guard.

units.zh: 藺五歲，每父母未飯，乳媼欲令藺先飯，藺曰：「旣不覺饑。」
units.en: At five, if his parents had not eaten the nurse would feed Lan first; he said, "I do not yet feel hungry."
units.literal: At five, whenever his parents had not yet eaten, the wet nurse wished to let Lan eat first; Lan said, "I am not yet aware of hunger."

units.zh: 強食終不進。
units.en: Pressed, he still would not eat.
units.literal: Though pressed he would in the end not eat.

units.zh: 舅阮孝緒聞之，歎曰：「此兒在家則曾子之流，事君則藺生之匹。」
units.en: His uncle Ruan Xiaoxu sighed, "At home this boy is like Zengzi; in serving a lord he would match young Lan."
units.literal: His maternal uncle Ruan Xiaoxu heard of it and sighed, "This child at home is of Zengzi's sort; in serving his lord he would match the lad Lan."

units.zh: 因名之曰藺。
units.en: So he was named Lan.
units.literal: He therefore gave him the name Lan.

units.zh: 稍受以經史，過目便能諷誦。
units.en: Taught the classics and histories, he could chant from memory whatever he read.
units.literal: Gradually he received instruction in the classics and histories; what passed before his eyes he could chant from memory.

units.zh: 孝緒每曰「吾家陽元也」。
units.en: Xiaoxu often said, "He is our house's Yangyuan."
units.literal: Xiaoxu often said, "He is the Yangyuan of our house."

units.zh: 及丁父憂，晝夜號慟，毀瘠骨立，母阮氏常自守視譬抑之。
units.en: After his father's death he wailed day and night until only bone remained; his mother Lady Ruan constantly watched and restrained him.
units.literal: When he entered mourning for his father he wailed day and night, wasted away until only bone stood, and his mother Lady Ruan constantly watched over him herself to restrain and comfort him.

units.zh: 服闋後，吏部尚書蕭子顯表其至行，擢爲王府法曹行參軍，累遷外兵記室參軍。
units.en: When mourning ended Minister Xiao Zixian recommended his utmost conduct; he became princely legal affairs gentleman, then outer staff recorder.
units.literal: After mourning he was recommended for utmost conduct by Minister of Personnel Xiao Zixian and was promoted court gentleman for legal affairs on the prince's staff, then in succession outer staff recorder.

units.zh: 時甘露降士林館，藺獻頌，高祖嘉之，因有詔使制《北兗州刺史蕭楷德政碑》，又奉令制《宣城王奉述中庸頌》。
units.en: When sweet dew fell on the Scholars' Grove, Lan presented a eulogy the emperor praised; he was ordered to compose the stele on Xiao Kai's virtuous rule in North Yanzhou and the eulogy on the Prince of Xuancheng presenting the Mean.
units.literal: At that time sweet dew fell on the Scholars' Grove; Lan presented a eulogy and Gaozu praised it, whereupon an edict ordered him to compose the Stele on the Virtuous Government of Xiao Kai, Inspector of North Yanzhou, and he was also ordered to compose the "Eulogy on the Prince of Xuancheng's Presentation of the Mean."

units.zh: 太清元年，遷散騎侍郎，兼散騎常侍，使於魏。
units.en: In Taiqing year one he became Gentleman Attendant and Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and envoy to Wei.
units.literal: In the first year of Taiqing he was promoted Gentleman Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and concurrently Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and sent as envoy to Wei.

units.zh: 會侯景舉地入附，境上交兵，藺母慮不得還，感氣卒。
units.en: When Hou Jing defected and border fighting broke out, Lan's mother feared he would not return and died of grief.
units.literal: When Hou Jing surrendered territory and came over, fighting broke out on the borders; Lan's mother feared he could not return and died of grief.

units.zh: 及藺還入境，爾夕夢不祥，旦便投劾馳歸。
units.en: On re-entering the realm that night he dreamed ill omens; at dawn he resigned and raced home.
units.literal: When Lan returned and entered the realm, that very evening he dreamed ill omens; at dawn he submitted his resignation and raced home.

units.zh: 旣至，號慟嘔血，氣絕久之，水漿不入口。
units.en: Arriving, he wailed until he vomited blood and long lost breath, and took no food.
units.literal: When he arrived he wailed and vomited blood and long lost breath; he would not take water or gruel.

units.zh: 親友慮其不全，相對悲慟，強勸以飲粥。
units.en: Kin feared he would not live and wept together, forcing thin gruel on him.
units.literal: Kin and friends feared he would not survive and mourned together; they forced him to take thin gruel.

units.zh: 藺初勉強受之，終不能進，經月餘日，因夜臨而卒，時年三十八。
units.en: He forced himself at first but could not swallow; after more than a month he died one night at the tomb, aged thirty-eight.
units.literal: At first Lan forced himself to accept it but in the end could not swallow; after more than a month, one night at the tomb he died, aged thirty-eight.

units.zh: 藺所制詩賦碑頌數十篇。
units.en: Lan composed several tens of poems, rhapsodies, steles, and eulogies.
units.literal: Lan composed several tens of pieces of poetry, fu, steles, and eulogies.

units.en: Marker denoting the historian's commentary section in the source text.
units.literal: Commentary section marker in the source text.

units.zh: 史臣曰：孔子稱「毀不滅性」，教民無以死傷生也，故制喪紀，爲之節文。
units.en: The historian says: Confucius said "grief must not destroy one's nature," teaching people not to harm life through death; hence mourning rules and ritual restraint were ordained.
units.literal: The historian says: Confucius said "grief should not destroy one's nature," teaching the people not to harm life through death; therefore mourning regulations were made and ritual texts set for restraint.

units.zh: 高柴、仲由伏膺聖教，曾參、閔損虔恭孝道，或水漿不入口，泣血終年，豈不知創鉅痛深，《蓼莪》慕切？
units.en: Gao Chai and Zhong You followed the sage; Zeng Shen and Min Sun were reverently filial—some took no food, some wept blood a year: did they not know wound and longing in "Luxuriant Reeds"?
units.literal: Gao Chai and Zhong You embraced the sage's teaching; Zeng Shen and Min Sun were reverently filial—some did not take water or gruel, some wept blood a full year: did they not know the wound was deep and the mourning in "Luxuriant Reeds" keen?

units.zh: 所謂先王制禮，賢者俯就。
units.en: So when the former kings made ritual, worthies bowed to it.
units.literal: This is what is meant when the former kings made ritual and worthies bow to it.

units.zh: 至如丘、吳，終於毀滅。
units.en: Men such as Qiu and Wu ended in self-destruction.
units.literal: As for Qiu and Wu, they ended in self-destruction.

units.zh: 若劉曇淨、何炯、江紑、謝藺者，亦二子之志歟。
units.en: Were Liu Tanjing, He Jiong, Jiang Gou, and Xie Lan not of that same intent?
units.literal: If Liu Tanjing, He Jiong, Jiang Gou, and Xie Lan are considered, are they not of those two men's intent?

units.zh: 後爲晉平王左常侍，遷司空桂陽王行參軍，隨齊司空柳世隆守郢城，拒荊州刺史沈攸之。
units.en: He became regular attendant to the Prince of Jinping, then staff officer to the Prince of Guiyang under the Minister of Works, and followed Liu Shilong in the defense of Yingcheng against Shen Youzhi.
units.literal: Later he was Regular Attendant to the Prince of Jinping, then a staff officer on the Prince of Guiyang's suite under the Minister of Works; he followed Qi Minister of Works Liu Shilong in holding Yingcheng against Jingzhou Inspector Shen Youzhi.

units.zh: 攸之平，遷前軍中兵參軍。
units.en: After Youzhi's defeat he was made army aide of the van.
units.literal: When Youzhi was pacified, he was promoted to Army Aide of the Van.

units.zh: 沖母，梁武帝妹新安穆公主，卒於齊世，武帝以沖偏孤，深所鍾愛。
units.en: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, a sister of Emperor Wu of Liang. She died in Qi times, and the emperor, seeing that Chong had been left partially orphaned, doted on him.
units.literal: Chong's mother was Princess Xin'an Mu, sister of Emperor Wu of Liang; she died in Qi times, and the Emperor, because Chong was a lone orphan, cherished him deeply.

units.zh: 按梁武帝即位後，追尊其父為文皇帝。
units.en: After Liang Wudi's accession he honored his father posthumously as Emperor Wen.
units.literal: According to the note, after Emperor Wu of Liang took the throne he posthumously honored his father as Emperor Wen.

units.zh: 王沖傳言其母為梁武帝妹新安穆公主，與此合。
units.en: Wang Chong's biography says his mother was Liang Wudi's sister Princess Xin'an Mu, which matches.
units.literal: The biography of Wang Chong says his mother was Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess Xin'an Mu—this agrees.

units.zh: 王沖 王通弟勱 袁敬兄子樞
units.en: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu
units.literal: Wang Chong; Wang Tong, younger brother Mo; Yuan Jing, nephew Shu

units.zh: [2]琳，齊代娶梁武帝妹義興長公主，有子九人，嵭知名。
units.en: Lin, in Qi times, married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister, Princess of Yixing long; he had nine sons, all of whom won notice.
units.literal: Lin, in Qi times married Emperor Wu of Liang's sister Princess of Yixing long, had nine sons, and all became renowned.

units.zh: 大同末，梁武帝謁園陵，道出朱方，勱隨例迎候，队勱令從輦側，所經山川，莫不顧問，勱隨事應對，咸有故實。
units.en: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs by way of Zhufang; Mo met him as custom required. The emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; at every hill and stream he asked questions, and Mo answered each with historical precedent.
units.literal: Near the end of Datong, Emperor Wu of Liang visited the imperial tombs; the route passed through Zhufang; Mo greeted him per custom; the Emperor ordered Mo to ride beside the carriage; every mountain and river passed, the Emperor inquired; Mo answered each matter with historical precedent.

units.zh: 尚書敬顯儁曰：「孔子云：『微管仲，吾其被發左衽矣』以此言之，右衽為是。」
units.en: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."
units.literal: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."

units.zh: 以如意擊幾自樂，皆有處所，時人方之閔子騫、原憲焉。
units.en: He struck the table with his ruyi scepter for his own pleasure, each stroke falling in its place; people of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.
units.literal: He struck the table with his ruyi scepter for his own pleasure, each stroke falling in its place; people of the time compared him to Min Ziqian and Yuan Xian.

units.zh: 夫曾參以布衣猶難之，今陛下親以王者修之，過曾參遠矣。
units.en: Even Zeng Shen, a commoner, struggled to match such devotion; you did it as heir to a kingdom—you have outdone Zeng Shen by a wide margin.
units.literal: Even Zeng Shen in plain cloth still found that hard; now Your Majesty, in the person of a king, practiced it—you surpass Zeng Shen by far.

units.zh: 初爲廷尉正，冬服單薄，寺卿蔡法度謂人曰：「我願解身上襦與顧郎，恐顧郎難衣食者。」
units.en: When he first served as Director of the Court of Justice, his winter clothing was thin. Director Cai Fadu of the bureau said to others, "I would gladly take off my own jacket and give it to Master Gu, but I fear he would find it hard to accept clothing and food."
units.literal: When he first served as Director of the Court of Justice, his winter clothing was thin. Director Cai Fadu of the bureau said to others, "I would gladly take off my own jacket and give it to Master Gu, but I fear Master Gu would find it hard to accept clothing and food."

units.zh: 晉世王公貴人，多葬梅嶺，及彭卒，叔陵啟求於梅嶺葬之，乃發故太傅謝安舊墓，棄去安柩，以葬其母。
units.en: In Jin many nobles were buried at Meiling; when Peng died Shuling asked to bury her there, opened Grand Tutor Xie An's old tomb, cast out An's coffin, and laid his mother in the grave.
units.literal: In Jin times many lords and nobles were buried at Meiling; when Peng died, Shuling memorialized asking to bury her at Meiling. He then opened the old tomb of Grand Tutor Xie An, cast out An's coffin, and buried his mother there.

units.zh: 謝太傅晉朝佐命，草創江左，斲棺露骸，事驚聽視。
units.en: Grand Tutor Xie had aided Jin in founding the realm and shaping the southeast; to break open his coffin and bare his bones horrified all who heard.
units.literal: Grand Tutor Xie aided Jin in founding the mandate and helped create the southeast; to chop open the coffin and expose the bones shocked every ear and eye.

units.zh: 又嘗詣徵士何胤，時太守衡陽王亦造焉，胤言之於王，王欲見荔，荔辭曰：「未有板刺，無容拜謁。」
units.en: He once visited the recluse He Yin. The Prince of Hengyang, then administrator, also came; Yin spoke of Li to the prince, who wished to see him. Li declined: "I have no visiting tablet and cannot pay respects."
units.literal: He also once visited the recluse He Yin; at the time the Administrator, the Prince of Hengyang, also came, and Yin spoke of him to the prince; the prince wished to see Li, but Li declined, saying: "I have no visiting tablet and cannot pay respects."

units.zh: 沈炯 虞荔 弟寄 馬樞
units.en: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; younger brother Ji; Ma Shu
units.literal: Shen Jiong; Yu Li; younger brother Ji; Ma Shu

units.zh: 昔晉武帝策荀公曾曰「周之冢宰，今之尚書令也」。
units.en: In former days Emperor Wu of Jin, in his edict to Xun Gongzeng, said: "The steward of Zhou is today's director of the masters of writing."
units.literal: In former days Emperor Wu of Jin, in his edict to Xun Gongzeng, said: "The steward of Zhou is today's Director of the Masters of Writing."

units.zh: 時武陵王在東州，頗自驕縱，上召革面敕曰：「武陵王年少，臧盾性弱，不能匡正，欲以卿代爲行事。
units.en: Prince Wuling held East Yangzhou and had grown proud and loose. The emperor summoned Ge and charged him in person: "Prince Wuling is young. Zang Dun is mild and cannot correct him. I want you to replace him as acting administrator.
units.literal: Prince Wuling was in East Yangzhou and rather arrogant and unrestrained; the Emperor summoned Ge and personally charged him: "Prince Wuling is young; Zang Dun is timid by nature and cannot correct him—I wish to have you replace him as acting administrator.

units.zh: 又載：周廣順中，張昭修實錄，奏云：梁末帝之上，有郢王友珪，篡弑居位，未有紀錄，請依《宋書》劉劭例，書為「元凶友珪」。
